Title: Senior Data Engineer
Description: Your Team Responsibilities The Senior Data Engineer will work in a fast-paced, collaborative environment, engaging with investment and technology professionals both within MSCI and across external organizations. The team is responsible for establishing and maintaining data feeds with custodian banks and data vendors, developing scalable data integration solutions, and supporting business growth through automation and process optimization. Senior Data Engineers are expected to demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a proactive, entrepreneurial mindset. Successful candidates will be comfortable working independently and collaboratively, managing multiple priorities, and leveraging emerging technologies to continuously improve data workflows and operational efficiency. Your Key Responsibilities Establish and maintain data feeds with custodian banks, data vendors, and other third-party service providers to support reliable integration of investment data. Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, with hands-on experience in data processing, analysis, and workflow automation. Solid understanding of data modeling, data quality, and database concepts, with the ability to work with large and complex datasets. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to independently investigate issues and develop effective solutions. Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt to evolving business and technical requirements. Familiarity with modern AI tools and experience leveraging AI-assisted development to improve efficiency, automation, and productivity. Eagerness to learn new technologies, explore innovative solutions, and continuously improve existing processes. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, or a related field. Experience with Snowflake, Databricks, Apache Airflow, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) is a plus. Master's degree in a relevant discipline preferred. Knowledge of financial markets is preferred. CFA charterholders or candidates pursuing the CFA designation are a plus. Title: ANALISTA COMERCIAL
Description: Objetivo del Puesto Asegurar la generación, análisis y seguimiento de información comercial clave para optimizar la toma de decisiones, impulsando el crecimiento de ventas, la rentabilidad y la eficiencia operativa de los talleres. Este rol contribuye directamente a los objetivos estratégicos mediante el monitoreo constante de indicadores críticos (venta, margen, catálogo, inventario y abastecimiento), la detección proactiva de oportunidades o riesgos, y la ejecución de acciones que garanticen la disponibilidad de producto y el mejor desempeño comercial del catálogo. Responsabilidades Principales Análisis de Indicadores (KPIs): Monitorear y reportar métricas de venta, margen de utilidad y rotación de inventarios para identificar desviaciones. Optimización de Catálogo: Evaluar el desempeño de los productos actuales y proponer ajustes para mejorar la oferta comercial. Gestión de Abastecimiento: Colaborar con los talleres para asegurar que los niveles de inventario sean óptimos, evitando quiebres de stock o excesos. Eficiencia Operativa: Detectar cuellos de botella en la operación comercial y proponer soluciones que maximicen la rentabilidad. Toma de Decisiones Basada en Datos: Traducir datos complejos en recomendaciones accionables para los líderes de área. Competencias Técnicas Capacidad de Análisis y Juicio: Habilidad para interpretar grandes volúmenes de datos y transformarlos en insights estratégicos. Mentalidad Innovadora: Apertura para proponer nuevas formas de trabajo y mejorar los procesos actuales. Agilidad de Aprendizaje: Capacidad para asimilar rápidamente nuevas herramientas tecnológicas y dinámicas del mercado e-commerce.

Title: LATAM Corporates - Consumer & Retail, Associate Director (Monterrey)
Description: LATAM Corporates – Consumer & Retail, Associate Director (Monterrey) Fitch is seeking an Associate Director for coverage of the Consumer & Retail sector based out of our Monterrey office. As one of the world’s top three credit ratings agencies, Fitch Ratings plays a critical role in global capital markets by providing supplementary credit analysis, ratings, research, and commentary to financial market participants. For over 100 years, Fitch Ratings has been creating value for global markets through its rigorous analysis and deep expertise, which have resulted in a variety of market leading tools, methodologies, indices, research, and analytical products. Fitch Ratings is part of Fitch Group, a global leader in financial information services with operations in more than 30 countries, which also includes Fitch Solutions. With dual headquarters in London and New York, Fitch Group is owned by Hearst. Joining Fitch Ratings in LATAM offers the opportunity to work with the most celebrated credit ratings organization in the region, renowned for its excellence and leadership. We boast a track record of over four decades of experience, with more than 2,000 ratings assigned to Latin American banks, corporates, structured finance, sovereigns and other entities. We cover the most relevant capital markets, showing a deep-rooted understanding of the region's unique financial environment. Our team is committed to innovation and collaboration, providing a dynamic environment where you can make a difference. Learn More: https://careers.fitch.group/go/Ratings-LATAM/9772901/ Qualitative credentials will weigh meaningfully in the selection of the candidate. A healthy sense of intellectual curiosity is critical, along with a willingness and ability to attack and explain topics of analytical complexity. Fitch is a team-oriented work environment, so excellent communication skills are essential, as is a high productivity work-ethic and results oriented mindset. What We Offer An opportunity to be a lead coverage analyst in the LATAM Consumer & Retail team at a global rating agency. A team-oriented work environment. Fitch Ratings is a global company with a presence in over 30 countries, offering opportunities to work with diverse teams and clients from around the world. We’ll Count On You To Perform analysis of key quantitative and qualitative factors influencing the credit quality of companies in the LATAM Consumer & Retail team. Develop and maintain comprehensive financial models. Present analysis of companies to internal credit rating committees. Conduct meetings with LATAM Consumer & Retail industry management teams. Involvement in communicating rating rationale to external audiences (primarily institutional investors, sell-side analysts and media) in meetings, conference calls, press releases and written research reports. Write timely and effective research on topical issues. Participate in the evaluation of other credits within the Consumer & Retail team, as well as other related credit groups. Represent Fitch in panel discussions and conferences arranged by industry associations, regulatory bodies etc. Mentor junior members of the LATAM Consumer & Retail team. Participate in meetings with Consumer & Retail industry executive-level management teams to strengthen understanding of their business and industry. What You Need To Have Bachelor's degree at minimum, MBA or other advanced degree a plus; 5+ years of relevant experience, which must include some coverage or knowledge of the Retail & Consumer sectors; Capital markets and/or credit analysis experience a plus; Strong analytical, quantitative, and organizational skills; Excellent written and verbal communication skills; Ability to shift fluidly between multiple projects as priorities change; Ability to excel in a team-oriented environment; Advanced English proficiency (verbal and written); Native Spanish speaker or advanced Spanish proficiency (verbal and written); Expertise in Excel and Word; CFA candidate preferred, CFA/CPA a plus. What Would Make You Stand Out A deep understanding of and a keen interest in the Consumer, Food & Beverage, Agriculture, Protein and Retail sectors; A professional background in capital markets and/or credit analysis and well-developed financial statement analysis and modeling skills; A strong pattern of leadership and the ability to proactively and successfully interact with various stakeholders, both within and outside of the organization. Intelligent solutions are increasingly part of our day-to-day operations, helping teams work more efficiently and think differently as we continue to evolve. We’re looking for colleagues who are comfortable operating in an AI-enabled environment—or who are curious, adaptable, and eager to build their AI literacy over time. We value professionals who embrace technology as part of continuous learning and who are committed to using it thoughtfully to enhance how work gets done. Fitch is committed to providing global securities markets with objective, timely, independent and forward-looking credit opinions. To protect Fitch’s credibility and reputation, our employees must take every precaution to avoid conflicts of interest or any appearance of a conflict of interest. Should you be successful in the recruitment process at Fitch Ratings you will be asked to declare any securities holdings and other potential conflicts prior to commencing employment. Title: Human Data Quality Analyst, AI Business
Industries: Construction, Software Development, and IT Services and IT Consulting
Description: Prolific Prolific isn’t just enabling AI innovation – we’re redefining it. While foundational AI technologies are becoming commoditized, Prolific’s human data infrastructure provides the high-quality, diverse data required to train the next generation of AI models. Through our platform, we empower researchers and companies to access a global, ethically curated participant base, ensuring cutting-edge AI research and training grounded in inclusivity and precision. The Role Prolific provides the human data that powers the next generation of AI models, working with frontier labs to capture the complex human judgments researchers need to train, evaluate and improve them. As a Human Data Quality Analyst, you'll be on the front line of making sure that data captures the right signal and is genuinely good enough to do its job. This isn’t traditional, back-office QA. You’ll be doing real analytical work: digging into datasets, identifying patterns and failure modes, investigating why quality has shifted, and turning complex findings into clear insights that help us improve how data is collected, reviewed and delivered. You'll spend real time reading annotations closely, but that is how you gather evidence, not what you produce. What you produce is analysis, practical recommendations and better quality controls. You'll get hands-on exposure to human data, annotation, machine learning pipelines and AI evaluation, working alongside Quality, Engineering, Operations and Delivery on new and evolving problems. There won't always be an established playbook. You'll be guided by our quality engineers, but you'll also need to run your own analysis, test your assumptions and recognise when you need input. It is a role with a steep learning curve from day one and a strong opportunity for someone early in their career to build deep, practical experience in a fast-moving area of AI. What You’ll Be Doing Run day-to-day quality measurement across live human-data programmes, combining statistical analysis with regular hands-on review to determine whether the data is fit for its intended use. Find the signal behind quality issues by investigating changes, quantifying their impact and distinguishing individual errors from wider problems in guidance, task design, training or tooling. Help build the data-quality pipeline alongside our quality engineers, turning repeated analysis into reliable validations and automated systems, including rule-based, LLM, and ML assisted approaches. Turn complex analysis into a clear story through reporting and visualisations that help stakeholders understand what is happening, why it matters, and what action the evidence supports. Support new programmes from design through to launch by helping develop the rubrics, guidelines, gold sets, calibration exercises, and production gates to measure quality from the start. Use what we learn from live programmes to improve annotation design, guidance, training and quality processes, then measure whether those changes work. What You’ll Bring to the Role You have 1 to 2 years of practical experience analysing real data in an analytical, quality, research or data-focused role. You can use SQL and Python to write your own queries and analysis, check whether the results make sense, and explain how you reached them. You can apply statistical concepts such as sampling, distributions and variability, and judge whether a result reflects a meaningful pattern or limited evidence. You can turn evidence into a clear account of what is happening, supported by concrete examples and practical recommendations that non-technical colleagues can act on. You can assess detailed work carefully and consistently while looking for patterns across the wider dataset, process or programme. When the right method is unclear, you can test a sensible approach, document your reasoning and recognise when you need input. Even Better if you have Experience working with data produced or judged by people, such as annotation, data labelling, research coding, content review or survey research, including measures such as agreement, gold-set accuracy or defect rates. Knowledge of psychology, behavioural science, linguistics or a related field, particularly how people interpret meaning and make judgements. An understanding of how human data supports model training and evaluation, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), preference data and evaluation benchmarks. Experience creating clear data visualisations or dashboards that help people understand and act on findings. Why Prolific is a great place to work We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems. We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviors into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breath and the best of humanity. Working for us will place you at the forefront of AI innovation, providing access to our unique human data platform and opportunities for groundbreaking research. Join us to enjoy a competitive salary, benefits, and hybrid working within our impactful, mission-driven culture. At Prolific, our compensation packages for eligible roles include base salary, equity, and benefits. Many roles also include the opportunity to earn a cash variable element, such as a bonus or commission. Your recruiter will also be happy to share the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Links to More Information Website Youtube Privacy Statement By submitting your application, you agree that Prolific may collect your personal data for recruiting and global organisation planning. Prolific's Candidate Privacy Notice explains what personal information Prolific may process, where Prolific may process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Prolific use of your personal information.

Title: Analista actuarial Jr - Reservas técnicas
Description: ¿Qué estamos buscando? Buscamos un perfil con sólida base analítica, rigor matemático y entusiasmo por consolidarse en el sector asegurador. Te integrarás a nuestro equipo actuarial para apoyar en la ejecución, control y análisis de reservas técnicas , participando activamente en los procesos de cierre mensual y colaborando en la consolidación de cifras de la compañía. Principales responsabilidades Apoyo en valuación de reservas: Ejecutar y dar seguimiento a los procesos mensuales para el cálculo de reservas técnicas (LRC y LIC) en ramos de vida, accidentes personales, salud o daños, asegurando la entrega en tiempo y forma para la consolidación financiera del Grupo. Calidad de datos y controles: Participar en la validación, limpieza y conciliación de bases de datos para garantizar la consistencia, suficiencia y exactitud de los insumos requeridos en la estimación de pasivos. Modelado y parametrización: Colaborar en la actualización, documentación y corrida de modelos actuariales/estadísticos e hipótesis (mortalidad, siniestralidad, persistencia), alineados al comportamiento operativo de la cartera. Documentación y soporte a auditorías: Asistir en la generación de reportes técnicos, papeles de trabajo y conciliaciones numéricas necesarias para atender los requerimientos de auditores internos, externos y reguladores. Colaboración interdisciplinaria: Atender requerimientos de información y conciliar cifras operativas con las áreas de Finanzas, Riesgos, Contabilidad y Sistemas. Retos del puesto El principal desafío de la posición radica en asimilar con agilidad la curva de aprendizaje de las metodologías de valuación técnica del sector, manteniendo un alto nivel de rigor analítico, orden y concentración durante los esquemas de alta presión típicos de los periodos de cierre operativo mensual. Asimismo, el rol exige desarrollar la capacidad de interpretar variaciones en las reservas para estructurar y comunicar resultados de forma clara, colaborativa y accesible ante auditores y áreas no técnicas de la organización. Requisitos del perfil. Conocimientos indispensables: Sólidas bases conceptuales en matemáticas financieras, cálculo actuarial, estadística y probabilidad. Comprensión de los principios básicos y funcionamiento de reservas técnicas en el sector asegurador. Manejo intermedio a avanzado de herramientas para el procesamiento de datos: Excel avanzado, sumado a conocimientos prácticos en SQL, Python o R para extracción y análisis de información. Conocimientos deseables: Nociones o familiaridad con la norma IFRS17 (cálculos de LRC/LIC, flujos descontados) o Solvencia II (Deseable / Plus valorado). Conocimiento general de normativas contables como US GAAP o regulación local de seguros. Nivel de inglés intermedio (lectura e interpretación de manuales técnicos y normativas). Escolaridad: Licenciatura concluida (titulado/a o pasante) en Actuaría, Matemáticas Aplicadas, Estadística, Economía o disciplinas cuantitativas afines. Experiencia: Mínima de 1 a 2 años de experiencia realizando funciones de análisis actuarial, valuación de reservas o modelado estadístico dentro del sector asegurador, reasegurador o firmas de consultoría. Title: Data Engineer
Description: About Ford And ATP Ford Motor Company has endured and thrived for more than 118 years by reimagining how things are built. Our job is not to deploy isolated tools; it is to build a system that learns from factory truth, transforms it into scalable platforms, and turns those platforms into enterprise business value. Advanced Industrial Technology and Platforms (ATP) is a new, centralised organisation designed to position Ford to lead industrial innovation. This team will accelerate our digital evolution and manufacturing excellence — advancing the modernisation of our Ford Manufacturing operations with cutting-edge technology. As part of Ford Manufacturing, ATP is designed to integrate directly into our manufacturing sites, partner across teams (GME, safety, etc.) and drive innovation from initial idea to full implementation. ATP is led by Managing Director Yung Fung, reporting to Ford Chief Manufacturing Officer Bryce Currie. This structure includes four vertical business units — focused on specific technology stacks — and four horizontals — shared services designed to ensure scale, deployment, and operational consistency. As part of the AITP organisation, the Sight Vertical is responsible for building an end-to-end business around AI/ML anomaly detection products, operating as two product families. Sight.Sense detects anomalies in parametric data: Sense.Machine (MiniTerms) for machine performance anomaly prediction and optimisation; Sense.Tooling (AI ToolSense) for tooling life optimisation; Sense.Energy for optimisation of supplies consumption; Sense.Stamping for stamping process anomaly prediction and surface splits; and Sense.MILO for in-process test quality anomaly detection. Sight.Vision detects anomalies in image data: Vision.Scout for in-station visual error proofing across manual and automated processes; Vision.Surface for surface defect detection in components and vehicle bodies through the complete manufacturing process; and Vision.Station for manual process monitoring and anomaly detection covering productivity, quality and ergonomics. The Sight Vertical product portfolio are set to converge on the Sight Anomaly Platform, which builds on Ford's Core Systems layer (Core OS, CoreDS, Core AI and CoreApps/FPS+). Together they form Ford's scalable platform to deliver, process quality assurance, and zero-downtime, zero-defect manufacturing. How The Sight Vertical Works The Sight Vertical operates through value-focused, cross-functional product teams across two product families: Sight.Sense and Sight.Vision, each led by a Head of Product Family. Product Managers lead the product problem, desired outcome and priority. Engineers and product designers work with them to discover and deliver effective solutions. Engineering Managers retain people, capacity, technical-system and engineering-health accountability. This is a vertical-level role working across both product families. Priorities are agreed between the two Heads of Product and their Engineering Managers, so that your effort is directed by portfolio value. In addition, ATP Core provides the non-product engineering expertise the verticals depend on — enterprise standards, architecture, industrial controls, cybersecurity and platform guidance. This role holds a matrix reporting line into ATP Core to ensure alignment with those standards and ready access to that expertise. The Opportunity We are looking for a Data Engineer to build and operate the data foundations of the Sight portfolio — the pipelines that carry factory truth from PLCs, sensors, cameras and plant systems into a platform where anomalies can be detected reliably, at scale, across Ford's global manufacturing footprint. Sight data is genuinely hard: tens of thousands of monitored assets, billions of waveforms annually, high-volume image and video data from Vision.Scout, Vision.Surface and Vision.Station, event-driven and polled sources, mixed plant infrastructure, and legacy equipment that was never designed to be observed. Getting this right is what makes the models trustworthy — and model trust is what determines whether plants act on our products or ignore them. You will work at the intersection of operational technology, cloud data engineering and machine learning enablement, across both parametric data and image-based detection. This is a senior individual contributor role. As the senior data engineering voice in the Sight Vertical, you will set the data engineering standards others work to, mentor engineers working with Sight data, and be accountable for ensuring the data foundations do not depend on you personally to remain trustworthy. The Position You will report into the Sight Vertical Director, with a matrix reporting line into the ATP Core team. The Sight Vertical Director leads what you prioritise and holds performance and development accountability; ATP Core provides technical alignment, enterprise standards and access to non-product expertise. Working embedded within product streams across both families, you will partner with the Software Architect, Controls Engineer, Senior Software Engineer, Software Engineers, data scientists, the Launch and Deployment Engineers and plant controls teams. You will provide technical direction and mentorship to engineers on data-related work. This is a senior individual contributor position with indirect leadership expectations. You will work primarily on Google Cloud Platform, Ford's strategic cloud platform, and engage with CoreDS and Core AI as the strategic data and ML platform direction for the Sight Vertical. Requires availability to travel internationally on occasion to understand plant data sources at source. 4 Days On Site In GTBC FORD México (Naucalpan, México) Able to travel periodically to Europe and US. Build and Operate Data Pipelines Design, build, test and operate reliable ingestion and processing pipelines from plant OT sources — PLC event data, sensor streams, waveform captures, energy meters and image capture — into GCP. Work with both event-driven ('notifier') and polled ('questioner') acquisition models, adapting to plant-level infrastructure choices such as CrossPLC (Ford developed middleware), Node-RED, DeviceWise, HiveMQ. Build batch and streaming pipelines on GCP — Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud Run/Functions, Cloud Composer, BigQuery and Cloud SQL/PostgreSQL — with infrastructure and pipelines defined as code. Handle high-volume unstructured image and video data for Vision products, including object storage design, lifecycle and cost management, frame sampling and metadata indexing. Own pipelines through production operation: monitoring, alerting, cost, backfill, recovery and incident response. Data Modelling, Quality and Semantics Design and maintain data models and semantic layers that make anomaly detection data usable across products and plants — including the common data model that enables global interoperability and rapid replication. Implement data quality controls: validation, completeness, drift, latency and lineage — and make data health visible rather than assumed. Model plant, line, station, asset and tool hierarchies consistently across both product families, integrating with systems of record such as Maximo. Optimise storage, partitioning and query performance and cost in BigQuery. Define and design data set lifecycle, historical, archiving, and purging approaches. Enabling Analytics and Machine Learning Prepare and serve training and inference datasets for parametric and image-based anomaly detection models, including labelling and annotation workflows, dataset versioning and feature availability. Partner with data scientists on the MLOps path to production — reproducible datasets, versioning, monitoring and retraining triggers. Support edge inference requirements, ensuring data available on the machine matches what models were trained on. Build the datasets behind value evidence and dashboards used by plants, Product Managers and the ATP ledger. Governance, Security and Engineering Practice Apply Ford data governance, privacy, retention and cybersecurity requirements across OT and IT boundaries, working with the Controls Engineer where plant-floor constraints apply. Give particular attention to imagery of people, where Vision.Station monitors manual processes and ergonomics — applying privacy, consent, retention and works council requirements with HR, Legal and local plant leadership. Manage access and identity appropriately for plant, product and enterprise consumers of Sight data. Define and own reusable ingestion and onboarding patterns so adding a plant is configuration rather than a project. Set data engineering standards for the vertical — pipeline design, testing, documentation, naming, lineage and runbook expectations — and hold work to them through review. Mentor and coach engineers working with Sight data, pairing on complex pipeline and modelling problems and explaining trade-offs rather than simply supplying answers. Actively reduce single-person dependency on critical datasets and pipelines, ensuring at least one other engineer can maintain each of them. Lead technical design for significant data platform changes, producing options, trade-offs and architecture decision records with the Software Architect. Functional & Technical Knowledge Minimum Requirements Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent demonstrable experience. Typically 5+ years of hands-on data engineering experience, with a substantial track record of production pipelines and data platforms you have designed, built and operated at scale. Advanced SQL and strong Python, with the judgement to choose appropriate tools and patterns rather than defaulting to the familiar. Practical experience with a major cloud data platform — GCP required (BigQuery, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Composer). Experience with batch and streaming data processing and with orchestration tooling. Experience of data modelling for analytical and operational use, and of data quality and validation practice. Software engineering fundamentals: version control, automated testing, CI/CD (GitHub Actions), infrastructure as code. Ability to work with imperfect, real-world industrial data and to trace problems back to source. Demonstrable experience mentoring and growing other engineers — pairing, design and code review, technical coaching and knowledge transfer. Ability to lead complex technical work end to end under ambiguity, and to communicate data trade-offs clearly to product, plant and non-technical stakeholders. Fluent professional English. Team player, problem solver, agile way of working. Preferred Requirements Experience with time-series, high-frequency sensor or waveform data at scale. Experience with unstructured image or video data at scale, including annotation pipelines and dataset versioning for computer vision models. Experience with industrial and OT data sources — PLC tag data, OPC-UA, MQTT, Modbus, historians, SCADA, energy metering. Experience supporting ML workloads and MLOps (Vertex AI, Keras/TensorFlow, feature stores, model monitoring). Experience with dbt, Dataform, Terraform or equivalent transformation and infrastructure-as-code tooling. Familiarity with data governance and cataloguing in a large enterprise, and with OT/IT security segregation. Experience of data privacy requirements where imagery or video of people is processed. Experience acting as the senior or lead data engineer in a team, setting standards and owning a data platform's direction. Exposure to manufacturing systems (Maximo, MES, GDPS 2.0) or automotive and other high-complexity manufacturing. Additional European language (Spanish or German). Success in Role Sight data pipelines are reliable, monitored, documented and cost-effective, with data quality visibly managed. Onboarding a new plant or asset group to the data platform becomes a configuration exercise, not a bespoke build. Data scientists and engineers can access trustworthy, reproducible datasets without bespoke intervention. A consistent common data model and asset hierarchy is in place across Sight products, supporting global replication. Model performance is supported by demonstrable data lineage, labelling quality and drift monitoring. Data governance, access control, privacy and cybersecurity requirements are met across OT and IT boundaries. Data engineering standards and patterns you have defined are visibly used by other engineers across both product families. Engineers you mentor demonstrably grow in autonomy and quality on data work; you are not a permanent bottleneck. No critical dataset or pipeline depends on a single person. Title: FP&A - Credit Products & Strategic Planning
Description: About Nu Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services. Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability. Visit our Institutional Page About The Team Mexico FP&A is the finance partner of the Mexico business. We sit between the product, credit, growth and marketing teams and the country leadership, and our job is to make sure every bet the business makes is sized, challenged and reflected in the P&L before it is made. We are not a reporting team. We work hand in hand with Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta (deposits and transactional) and Growth stakeholders, as well as Treasury, Controllership, Public Policy, Second Line Risk and Investor Relations, to turn strategy into numbers and numbers into decisions. How We Work We are owners: we make things happen instead of waiting for them. We have a bias to output: fast, right-sized answers over months-long projects. We set the finance agenda, not only serve it. We embrace conflicting ideas and question the status quo, with data. We work hard, with integrity and putting the team first. About The Role As the IC7 in Mexico FP&A for credit products and strategic planning, you are the senior analytical bridge between Mexico's credit products, the P&L and the planning process. You do not run closings or own the budget calendar. You own something harder: making sure what goes into the plan is grounded, challenged and financially sound, and that leadership decides with the right numbers in front of them. The role has three faces. You are a business partner to Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core, who challenges their strategy and helps them bake initiatives into the plan. You are a first responder who quantifies, within days, anything that hits the P&L that wasn't planned. And you are a decision shaper who builds the frameworks, tools and governance leadership uses to decide. At this level you set the finance agenda rather than wait for requests. You work directly with the country CEO, CFO and business-unit leaders, move between hands-on modeling and executive framing in the same week, and raise the analytical bar of the team around you. What You Will Do Partner with product teams and bake their initiatives into the plan Understand the projections of Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core teams and challenge the strategy behind them: assumptions, timing, certainty and whether the impact is really incremental. Help teams translate initiatives into P&L impact when they don't know how, and carry them into budget, rebudget, forecast checkpoints and the 5-year plan. Size initiatives with a consistent toolkit (NPV, CAC, payback, ROAS, gross profit) and apply clear inclusion criteria. Push back when a plan doesn't add up and perform deep dives proactively, for example recommending not to launch a program until its economics are positive, and proposing alternatives such as phased rollouts or test budgets. React fast to anything that hits the P&L unplanned Be the first to quantify regulatory and market shocks. Turn the impact into options: mitigation levers, owners and dates, not only a number. Detect and escalate data and accounting anomalies that distort the P&L. Be the analytical bridge between credit products, the P&L and planning Challenge investments and strengthen how decisions are made with clear argumentation. Build tools leadership can use directly that help in the decision-making process. Propose and drive decision governance, especially on when Finance must be involved. Communicate to executives and raise the bar of the team Prepare materials for executives with a clear narrative, grounded in numbers. Support regulatory deliverables. Coach analysts on the team and set the bar for analytical rigor. What We Are Looking For Must have Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Actuarial Science or a related quantitative field; a master's degree is a plus. 8+ years of experience in FP&A, business analytics, strategy or credit analytics, with a significant part in consumer credit, banking or fintech. Track record of changing senior leadership decisions with analysis: stopping, reshaping or accelerating initiatives based on their economics. Deep unit-economics and credit knowledge: NPV, CAC and payback, ROAS and incrementality, cost of risk, provisions (IFRS 9), funds transfer pricing, interchange, and how credit policy flows into the P&L. Hands-on analytical skills: SQL, financial modeling and spreadsheets; Python or notebooks is a strong plus. You build your own data instead of waiting for it. Ability to lead cross-functional analyses end to end with Product, Credit, Treasury, Controllership, Risk and Public Policy, and to influence without authority. Executive communication: turn complex analysis into a one-page story and a clear recommendation for C-level audiences. Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you can size an unplanned impact in days and refine it later. Experience coaching or mentoring analysts. Fluency in Spanish and English. Title: Solutions Architect | LATAM
Description: Our Solutions Architecture team connects business priorities with practical technical solutions, helping customers understand how Chainalysis can support their most important objectives. In this role, you will provide technical leadership throughout the customer journey. You will turn complex requirements into clear recommendations, help customers envision how our products fit into their operating environment, and guide them toward measurable business outcomes. As a Solutions Architect, you'll develop a deep understanding of Chainalysis solutions and the problems our customers are trying to solve. You'll explain complex concepts in a clear, compelling way to technical practitioners, business leaders, and executive stakeholders. You'll also build practical, customer-specific solutions that support deployment, integration, adoption, and long-term value. In This Role, You'll Serve as a core member of the account team, partnering closely with Sales, Services, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering. Take ownership of customer outcomes across the full lifecycle, from initial discovery and solution design through investigation support, compliance program delivery, deployment, enablement, adoption, and expansion. Lead discovery conversations that uncover customer objectives, operational pain points, use cases, technical constraints, and success criteria. Translate business and operational needs into clear technical requirements, solution designs, and implementation paths. Articulate Chainalysis capabilities in a way that is relevant to each customer's compliance, risk, fraud, investigations, or security environment. Create tailored demonstrations, proof-of-value experiences, and technical narratives that show how Chainalysis can address customer priorities. Conduct blockchain investigations, deliver compliance and regulatory guidance, and build technical solutions such as notebooks, dashboards, automation workflows, data integrations, reference architectures, and agentic workflows. Develop AI-assisted workflows that accelerate and automate investigations, analysis, and customer processes, adapted to each customer's operating model, data, controls, and risk framework. Design automation that fits into existing compliance, risk, fraud, investigations, or security operations rather than requiring customers to redesign how they work. Help customers access and operationalize Chainalysis data through APIs, integrations, and fit-for-purpose technical patterns. Provide guidance on solution architecture, API implementation, workflow design, data movement, and integration considerations. Drive platform adoption by connecting customer workflows to Chainalysis capabilities and identifying new use cases. Identify creative, responsible approaches to difficult customer problems, while balancing speed, scalability, security, maintainability, and measurable impact. Build trust through sound technical judgment, clear communication, reliable execution, and a strong understanding of the customer's business. Assemble the technical evidence base, including outcome data, consumption metrics, adoption analysis, and expansion signals, that supports quarterly impact reporting and renewal conversations. Build customer capability and self-sufficiency rather than creating ongoing dependence on the Solutions Architecture team. Own the feedback loop between customers and Product/Engineering, translating field insights and feature requirements into product improvements and bringing those improvements back to customers. Act as a trusted advisor to customers, meeting them at their current level of crypto-maturity and partnering with them to advance their understanding, processes, and outcomes. Represent Chainalysis at customer meetings, industry events, and conferences. Contribute to the wider Solutions Architecture team through reusable assets, knowledge sharing, internal initiatives, and better ways of working. We're Looking For Candidates Who Have Several years of experience in one or more relevant areas, such as financial services, compliance, investigations, fraud, cybersecurity, digital assets, transaction monitoring, sales engineering, solutions architecture, or enterprise product management. Experience making complex technical or operational concepts understandable to different audiences. Strong storytelling, presentation, and written communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical teams and executive stakeholders. A creative, structured, and investigative approach to solving challenging customer problems. Comfort working with technical tools and learning new technologies quickly. Experience with Python or another programming language, SQL, data analysis, notebooks, workflow automation, APIs, integrations, or AI tools is valuable. The curiosity and initiative to develop technical depth over time; you do not need to arrive with a complete technical stack, but you should enjoy investigating how things work and building the skills to solve new problems. The ability to operate effectively when requirements are ambiguous, information is incomplete, or the best path forward has not yet been defined. A collaborative, generous approach to working with others, including a willingness to share knowledge, seek input, and improve team practices. A demonstrated focus on measurable customer outcomes, not simply technical activity or product usage. An interest in blockchain and a desire to keep building your understanding of the technology, the market, and the customers we serve. AI at Chainalysis AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it. AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before. About Chainalysis Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation. You belong here. At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture. We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. Title: Data Pipeline Engineer
Description: About the Team DoorDash is looking for an experienced Data Engineer to join our growing Tax Data Mart team. This role will be a key contributor to the team and will be responsible for building and operating the data pipelines and infrastructure that power analytics and decision-making across the company. As DoorDash continues to grow its global footprint across multiple business lines, we are looking for a candidate with experience designing and maintaining scalable data systems. This person will support and grow our unique community via your blend of engineering, technology, and process improvement experience. About the Role You will be reporting to the Manager of Tax Data Mart, and play an integral role in DoorDash's data function, owning the processes for ingesting, transforming, and controlling our data, ensuring accuracy, and making it available to analytics and business users. As a member of this team, you will lead the design, implementation, and operation of data pipelines and related processes to support the Company's exponential growth. You're excited about this opportunity because you will… Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable data pipelines (ETL/ELT) that serve data across the company Develop and optimize data models and warehouse structures to support analytics and reporting Participate in new business initiatives and identify their impact on existing data system(s) and processes. Work closely with Analytics, Data Science, and business partners in the development and validation of new data sources. Identify and document business, functional and technical requirements to support new business initiatives and to enhance existing system functionality. Leverage AI & AI assisted tooling to build and automate recurring data tasks & pipelines. Monitor data quality, reliability, and observability, and resolve data-related issues for our internal business partners. Participate in defining the Company's data tooling needs, including the maintenance of existing systems. Prepare documentation related to our data systems and processes. Share knowledge and best practices with engineers and analysts across the team. We're excited about you because… You have 5+ years of experience in a data engineering or similar role. Experience using Data Build Tool (DBT) or a similar product to manage data flows. Experience using Claude, Cursor and similar AI tools. You are an expert at using SQL with experience using Snowflake. Proficiency in Python (or a comparable language) for building data pipelines. Experience with modern data stack and orchestration tools such as Airflow, Spark, or Kafka. You have strong attention to detail and analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. You're an independently motivated person with a proven ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize work independently. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills. Project management experience, including creation of project plans, milestones, and due dates. Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related degree. Title: Supply Chain Resilience & Sub-Tier Risk Specialist
Description: Why Join Ford of Mexico? Celebrating over 100 years of legacy in Mexico, we are more than just a business we are a vibrant, collaborative community of over 14,000 innovators shaping the global future of transportation. At Ford, we build what matters, grow where it counts, and drive progress with heart. Whether you are collaborating at our state-of-the-art Global Technology and Business Center (GTBC) or manufacturing iconic, award-winning vehicles in our world-class plants, you will find a culture evolving together, built on trust, passion, and shared purpose. Here, your work moves people forward, and your growth is personal. Join us, and let’s build what’s next together. In this position... The Ford Purchasing team adds critical value to the entire organization. You’ll help us source the highest quality parts and services from around the globe while ensuring optimal cost and on-time delivery. You’ll also contribute to establishing a robust supply chain so that we can continually produce the vehicles our customers want. As a Supply Chain Resilience & Sub-Tier Risk Specialist , you will help strengthen the continuity of Ford’s global supply chain by identifying and reducing risks before they affect vehicle production. You will build visibility beyond direct suppliers, uncover potential material and supplier vulnerabilities, and partner with teams across purchasing, engineering, quality, and logistics to develop practical solutions. Your work will help protect customers, support responsible sourcing, and enable more reliable production across our business. What You'll Do... Map multi-tier supply networks for critical materials, components, and commodities to improve visibility beyond direct suppliers. Identify supply-chain vulnerabilities, including single-source dependencies, geographic concentration, capacity constraints, logistics disruptions, and raw-material availability risks. Analyze supplier, market, and operational data to assess potential production impacts and prioritize mitigation opportunities. Lead cross-functional working groups to develop and execute risk-reduction plans, such as qualifying alternate suppliers, validating substitute materials, or diversifying manufacturing locations. Create clear risk reports, dashboards, and executive updates that translate complex supply-chain information into actionable recommendations. Support proactive monitoring of supplier, commodity, logistics, and geopolitical trends to help prevent disruptions and strengthen long-term supply-chain resilience. You'll have... Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Logistics, Business, or a related field; or equivalent practical experience. Typically 5 to 8 years of experience in supply chain operations, procurement, supplier management, logistics, manufacturing, or supply-chain risk management. Experience analyzing multi-tier supplier networks, supplier dependencies, raw-material sourcing, supply disruptions, or business continuity risks. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional projects and influence stakeholders across purchasing, engineering, quality, manufacturing, and logistics. Experience using supply-chain visibility, risk-management, or supplier-mapping tools, such as Resilinc, Everstream, or similar platforms. Proficiency with data visualization and analysis tools such as Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or similar software. Working knowledge of product bills of materials, global logistics networks, international shipping terms, and North American trade requirements. Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to convert complex information into clear business recommendations. Spanish language proficiency is a plus. Even Better, You May Have A master’s degree, MBA, APICS or ASCM certification, commodity expertise in semiconductors, battery materials, or metals, and experience with enterprise resource planning platforms such as SAP or Oracle are preferred. Availability to work under a hybrid schedule at the corporate office Job Base Location - GTBC (Lomas Verdes, Naucalpan de Juarez - Estado de México) Ford of Mexico is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. Title: Lifecycle Cost Efficiency Analyst
Description: Join a team that shapes the financial DNA of every vehicle we build. As a Lifecycle Cost Efficiency Analyst, you'll play a pivotal role in achieving and sustaining world-class material cost performance across the full lifecycle of a vehicle nameplate. Partnering closely with Motion Tech Strategy, Tech Platform Planning, Finance, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams, you'll help ensure every dollar spent on our vehicles delivers maximum value to our customers and the company.
